findings.text: blocking: the fallback is triggered by counting per-run files naming a tree, so a tree named by exactly one per-run file and by a record living only in the aggregate crew.json is answered from the per-run file, while the whole-ledger scan attributes it to the last record by completion; the two disagree (repro-parity-divergence.log: HELD_fast r-...T090000000000-alpha-holds vs WHOLE r-...T100000000000-alpha-holds), sending a coordinator at the wrong run for a held tree. Latent today only because no inspected tree resolves through the fast path (fallback-share.log trees_from_file 0), but reachable once post-split runs accumulate held trees.

follow-on: the fragment's gate figures read "50 passed, 2 failed" (base) and "51 passed, 1 failed" (head), while the gate logs it cites read 51/2 and 52/1 at the same revision; the numbers were not regenerated after the ordering test was added.

findings_note: the mixed per-run-plus-aggregate divergence was reproduced at head by the reviewer under the run scratch (repro-parity-divergence.log)

item_verdicts.diff: read 64a56280f..44139f82e commit by commit; 40d66ddc1 replaces the whole-ledger load with a per-inspected-tree read selected from the run id (reckon/crew/obligations.py:334), 44139f82e adds the whole-ledger fallback for a tree more than one per-run file names (reckon/crew/obligations.py:341), 0adc145f1 and 9e2114a4d are the evidence fragment; the mixed per-run-plus-aggregate case is unhandled.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names a parity case (held set equals the whole-ledger derivation), a never-called case and a fallback case, recorded as base/head arms; tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py:175 asserts parity but its fixture never places one tree under both a per-run file and the aggregate, so the equality the gate asserts is weaker than the equality the code must hold.
item_verdicts.goal: read the node goal at prompt.txt ("obligations._held_worktrees no longer loads the whole ledger, and reads the per-run ledger file for each run whose worktree it inspects") and the landed change in reckon/crew/obligations.py:327-358: the per-run read lands, but a tree named by one per-run file and also by an aggregate-only record resolves to a different run than the whole-ledger scan.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the manifest: it records commits 40d66ddc1..44139f82e, the gate (base 2 failed 51 passed, head 1 failed 52 passed), parity over 25 sessions and two negative controls; it does not record the ruff gate its done-when names (I ran it at head: ruff check and ruff format --check both clean), and its fragment's gate counts lag those in the logs it cites.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest's orientation_write_paths and the diff agree — reckon/crew/obligations.py, tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py and docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/held-worktrees-read-run-files.html, with no path outside the grant and no plan edit.

justifications.durability: tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py:250 monkeypatches ledger.runs and ledger.load to raise and so would redden if the whole-ledger read returned, but the parity guard at tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py:175 cannot fail on the mixed per-run-plus-aggregate case that the divergence reproduces.
justifications.evidence: gate-base.log and gate-head.log name revisions 64a56280f21a10d8312b04fc3441373d1207e857 and 44139f82ee9efae1ff3b27c26d13c60cec4caf9c and exit 1 with one added-failure-free delta, parity-real-fleet.log compares 25 sessions with 0 mismatches and gate-negative-control-ordering.log shows the control red (2 failed) — but the parity case omits the mixed source, and the fragment's counts lag the logs.
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's existing helpers and mechanism-voice comments (reckon/crew/obligations.py:266 _names_worktree reads the same two fields as the whole-ledger scan) and introduces no plan, ticket or version label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/obligations.py:341 triggers the whole-ledger fallback only when a tree has no per-run file or more than one, so a tree named by one per-run file and by an aggregate-only record yields a different run id than the whole-ledger scan the goal's parity implies.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff touches only the three granted paths (reckon/crew/obligations.py, the new test file and the evidence fragment) and the naming checks over the added lines flag nothing.
